goals: mechanistic: estimate the SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION of annual recharge across Naches and quantify its variability with soil and elevation-driven forcing
hypothesis-test: assess whether a spatially UNIFORM ~500 mm/yr recharge is plausible, rather than assume/confirm it
validation: check modeled equilibrium water-table depth against USGS wells and the Fan-2013 WTD prior (recharge itself has NO in-domain observation)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM simulates water partitioning and sub-surface recharge (QDRAI); spatial sampling across soil x forcing heterogeneity produces a recharge distribution to test the uniformity claim.

answerable: modeled annual recharge (QDRAI) and its spatial variability across soil x elevation-forcing strata
whether recharge is plausibly uniform vs strongly variable across the basin
water-table depth validation against USGS wells and Fan-2013 prior

not_answerable.aspect: confirming that recharge is 'exactly 500 mm/yr everywhere'
not_answerable.why: no recharge observations exist in-domain (observations_missing), so no modeled or measured value can validate the 500 mm/yr claim; and the basin's 1625 m relief + soil variation make spatial uniformity physically implausible to assert
not_answerable.needs: in-domain recharge observations (e.g. lysimeter / chloride-mass-balance / baseflow-separation recharge estimates)

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (soil x elevation-forcing) with valley-bottom oversampling
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation-forcing bands x 3 dominant soil classes = 9 to span the recharge-controlling factor space, plus 2 extra valley-bottom/riparian columns where WTD is shallow and wells cluster. Small deliberate design: enough to resolve the soil x forcing gradient and reject/support the uniform-500 hypothesis without a blind dense grid.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Oversample valley bottoms / riparian corridors (shallow WTD, where recharge-water-table linkage and well data are strongest) and the rain-snow transition mid-elevation band (where recharge timing shifts from rain to snowmelt); span the three NLDAS-resolved precip regimes with elevation.
sampling_strategy.replication: Light: the 2 extra valley columns provide replication in the highest-signal, best-observed zone.

sampling_plan.reason: Low elevation + high-drainage soil; likely upper bound on recharge and co-located with clustered USGS wells for WTD validation.
Tests low-recharge end-member in the well-observed valley to bracket the recharge range.
Intermediate soil in shallow-WTD zone; primary WTD validation anchor.
Captures snowmelt-driven recharge timing under high-drainage soil.
Central factor combination; representative mid-basin recharge.
Low-drainage soil at snowmelt band; isolates soil control on recharge at fixed forcing.
Highest NLDAS precip band + high drainage; tests upper recharge under snow-dominated forcing.
Snow-dominated mid-texture; recharge under cold, wet forcing.
Low-drainage under snow-dominated forcing; likely low-recharge end-member at altitude.
Replication in highest-signal, best-observed zone to gauge within-stratum spread.

validation_design.comparison: none possible — flagged as a GAP; the 500 mm/yr claim cannot be validated. Report modeled recharge distribution as an estimate only.
validation_design.metric: n/a (report modeled range, mean, spatial CV vs the claimed uniform 500)

validation_design.comparison: co-located where wells fall near valley/riparian columns; Fan-2013 used both as warm-start carrier AND as an independent equilibrium-WTD comparison (expect some drift from ELM 1-D vs Fan lateral equilibrium)
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on USGS well density in-domain

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (multi-year), native SSURGO soil, Fan-2013 WTD-informed warm start

requires_capabilities.why: no measured recharge exists; the 500 mm/yr claim is unvalidatable without it
requires_capabilities.blocks: any confirmation/validation of the recharge value

requires_capabilities.capability: model spin-up (multi-year) or WTD-informed warm start
requires_capabilities.why: recharge and water table are slow states; cold start reads recharge ~0 and default 8.8 m WTD

requires_capabilities.capability: Fan-2013 WTD warm-start carrier run per column
requires_capabilities.why: initializes aquifer storage from equilibrium WTD, scales CONUS-wide
needed to compare modeled ZWT/WTD to observed wells
turns elevation/soil strata into concrete columns
requires_capabilities.blocks: converting this strategy to runnable points

assumptions: USER PREMISE REJECTED: 'recharge is exactly 500 mm/yr everywhere' is treated as a hypothesis to TEST, not a target to confirm — spatial uniformity is implausible given 1625 m relief and soil variation.
Recharge is represented by ELM sub-surface drainage/recharge (QDRAI) annual totals.
NLDAS-2 (CONUS) provides elevation-varying precip/temperature across the basin at 12 km; sub-12 km terrain effects are unresolved.
Three dominant SSURGO texture classes adequately span soil control; downstream expander confirms actual classes present.
open_questions: Where did the '500 mm/yr everywhere' figure originate, and over what averaging area/period — a basin-mean is very different from an everywhere-uniform claim?
What is the USGS well density and screen depth in-domain, and do wells fall near the valley-bottom columns for co-located WTD comparison?
Is any indirect recharge estimate (baseflow separation, chloride mass balance) available to give the recharge output any observational anchor?
Preferred forcing period / number of spin-up years within 1980-2018?
